finding.headline: At 51, you can now contribute more to your 401(k) each year, and the catch-up limit rises at 60.
details: For 2027, people aged 50 and over can contribute up to $34,000 a year to most 401(k) plans, with the catch-up limit at $8,500.
Once you reach age 60 through 63, the catch-up limit rises to $11,750, which applies to you in the years before your planned retirement at age 66.
Medicare starts at age 65, which is 14 years away. Sign up for Medicare at 65 even if you keep working past that age, or your coverage may cost more.

finding.headline: About 11% of your pay goes to tax now; about 4% of withdrawals in retirement.
details: Now you pay about $9,241 in tax on $86,500 of pay, leaving about $77,259.

Draw order: taxable and cash savings first, then the 401(k), and Roth accounts last. This is a rough guide, not tax advice.

assumptions: All figures are in today's dollars: what money buys now, not the larger sums prices will reach.

Savings grow on average 5.0% a year above inflation in stocks and 1.8% in bonds, with good and bad years. The plan tests many possible market paths. These are planning figures, not a forecast. They are fixed, so every plan is tested on the same markets; to see a bad stretch, try a What If such as markets fall 30%.
Until you retire you save about $259 a year: $259 of take-home pay left after your spending, which the plan assumes you save. If that is wrong, change 'Yearly saving' in your answers.
Pay stays at today's level until you retire, with no raises. This is fixed: raises are not certain, so the plan does not count on them. If your pay changes, change it in your answers.
Social Security uses the figure you gave, read as the benefit at 67. Your answers show $30,500 a year from 67. This plan starts it at 66, which pays about $28,500 a year.
If you retire before Medicare starts at 65, health cover costs about $10,000 a person a year until then (an assumption). Other health costs follow CMS figures by age.

Tax uses the 2027 federal brackets, the standard deduction and your state's rates. While you work, 401(k) saving comes off taxable pay and the child tax credit applies. In retirement the plan counts 85% of Social Security as taxable, the most the law allows, so the tax may be a little high.
The plan runs to age 92. There is about a 1 in 4 chance that you will live that long (US life table, SOA 2024). People with more money tend to live longer than that table says.
